title: Canonical reduction and augmentation of the completed regular coefficient unit
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, a finite-field datum D with different characteristic, and a scheme W where l is a unit in every stalk, there exists CompletedUnitPullback.Reduction l E W for the fixed calculus of [def-pur-completed-unit-pullback-data]. The finite identifications act as the identity on sections, their derived comparison uses the actual constantCoefficientReductionMap at every level, and the augmentation is the adjunction unit followed by the total limit of that comparison.

source.place: Sections 3.5 and 6.5, Lemmas 6.5.9 and 6.8.2; regular-module calculation in lem-pur-completed-unit-pullback-tower

proof.text: Construct finite identifications by inverse of the unit-to-pushforward-unit map along the equality of the evaluated ring and the actual finite ring. Their section formula follows by equality induction and the inverse equations. Apply the strict regular-system comparison. Existing constructibility gives derived completeness; stalkwise invertibility implies invertibility on global sections. Normalized reconstruction makes the actual adjunction unit invertible. Compose this unit isomorphism with total limit of the strict comparison; its augmentation equation holds by definition.

proof_origin.place: Explicit normalized regular-module argument, refined from the parent proof
